intro: Los Feliz sits at the foot of Griffith Park, with two walkable village streets, Hillhurst and Vermont, lined with cafes, old-school Italian spots, bookstores and a century-old movie palace. It's also the easiest way up to the Observatory and the Greek Theatre.

places.w: A minimalist espresso bar that many coffee people rank among the best in LA. The line moves faster than it looks.
places.o: The cream top or a vanilla latte. It's small, so plan to take it to go.

places.w: A two-story cafe at the bottom of Los Feliz with strong, espresso-heavy drinks and a friendly counter.
places.o: The house flat white with sweet cream. Card only.

places.w: A pair of historic bungalows with a big shaded patio, and Los Feliz's go-to brunch for decades. Breakfast runs until 5pm.
places.o: Something from the pastry case and a breakfast plate on the patio. Valet helps with parking.

places.w: A neighborhood cafe and bakery with one of the most talked-about breakfast burritos on the Eastside.
places.o: The breakfast burrito with both salsas.

places.w: A leafy patio cafe that overlooks the Los Feliz par-3 golf course. Calm and easy to park.
places.o: The breakfast burrito or salmon with poached eggs, then nine holes.

places.w: A big, friendly patio restaurant on Hillhurst that does everything from pancakes to burgers.
places.o: Banana walnut pancakes at brunch, or chicken and waffles.

places.w: A mostly outdoor all-day spot built on seasonal produce. Breakfast is casual; dinner gets lively.
places.o: A breakfast burrito by day, the dry-aged steak and a leafy salad at night.

places.w: A time-capsule Italian room that works from breakfast to a late dinner.
places.o: Ricotta pancakes in the morning; clams casino and the hanger steak at night.

places.w: A candlelit British restaurant that's become the hardest table in the neighborhood.
places.o: Bangers and mash with a natural wine. Book well ahead.

places.w: Bright Middle Eastern cooking that still sets the bar for dinner in Los Feliz.
places.o: Spicy pickles, the cauliflower and the crispy rice.

places.w: A stunning multi-level Mexican courtyard where the cocktails are the main event.
places.o: A mezcal cocktail and the tacos arabes.

places.w: A cozy, affordable red-sauce pasta standby.
places.o: The arrabbiata or the bolognese.

places.w: A charming French sidewalk cafe on Vermont.
places.o: The creamy polenta with a fried egg.

places.w: A bustling Paris-style bistro with a huge brunch menu and a sidewalk made for lingering.
places.o: A ham and cheese crepe and a cafe au lait.

places.w: One of LA's best smashburgers, right next to the Los Feliz 3 for a post-movie bite.
places.o: The California Classic.

places.w: A tiny roadside stand that's been feeding the neighborhood for about 50 years and won a James Beard award.
places.o: Cochinita pibil tacos and the cheeseburger.

places.w: A short menu of fish, shrimp and potato tacos on a thatched patio. Fast, cheap and reliable.
places.o: Fish tacos and a trip to the salsa bar.

places.w: A Texas-style taco counter known for breakfast tacos on fresh flour tortillas.
places.o: Breakfast tacos and the Frito pie in a bag.

places.w: Thick, square slices for about five dollars.
places.o: The classic tomato pie.

places.w: A hand roll counter for a quick, creative sushi lunch.
places.o: A set of three to six rolls.

places.w: An old-school Vermont Avenue diner with pie all day.
places.o: Pancakes or chicken pot pie, then a slice of cream pie.

places.w: A retro cocktail bar with a strong drink list and bistro snacks.
places.o: A Negroni made with vintage Campari.

places.w: A friendly wine bar where the staff pours by your taste instead of a long list.
places.o: Tell them what you like and add tinned fish.

places.w: A classic lounge and steakhouse with old-school cocktails and live music.
places.o: A martini in the lounge during the live set.

places.w: LA's Art Deco hilltop observatory, with free astronomy exhibits, a planetarium and the city's best sunset view.
places.o: Walk up the two-mile trail instead of driving, then stay for sunset and a planetarium show.

places.w: More than 4,000 acres of trails, canyons and picnic lawns right behind the neighborhood.
places.o: A morning hike from the Vermont side, then brunch on Hillhurst.

places.w: A 1929 open-air amphitheater in a canyon, and one of the best places in LA to see a summer show.
places.o: Walk or rideshare. The stacked parking can take longer than the concert.

places.w: A century-old single-screen movie palace with an Egyptian interior. Every other row was removed, so there's real legroom.
places.o: A matinee with real butter on the popcorn.

places.w: The neighborhood's other historic cinema, smaller and cheaper than the Vista.
places.o: A movie, then Goldburger next door.

places.w: A beloved independent bookstore with great staff picks, author readings and an art book annex next door.
places.o: Check the readings calendar.

places.n: Barnsdall Art Park and Hollyhock House
places.w: A hilltop park around Frank Lloyd Wright's Hollyhock House, with summer wine tastings and outdoor movies.
places.o: Tour the house, then catch the sunset from the lawn.

places.w: A historic public staircase that gives you a real workout on the way toward Griffith Park.
places.o: Do a few laps early in the morning.

places.n: Wacko and La Luz de Jesus Gallery
places.w: A pop-culture oddities shop that gets stranger the deeper you go, with a lowbrow art gallery in back.
places.o: Browse the gallery's current show.

places.n: Autry Museum of the American West
places.w: A big museum of the American West inside Griffith Park.
places.o: Pair it with a Griffith Park picnic.

places.w: A free outdoor railroad museum in Griffith Park where kids can climb on real trains.
places.o: Weekend morning with little kids.
